filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-01.question: In Philippians 4:11, Paul says he learned to live content in every situation.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-01.feedbackCorrect: Learned, not automatic: content in every situation.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Philippians 4:11: that is exactly what he declares.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-01.hint: See the verb "aprendi" in the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-02.question: In Philippians 4:12, tap how Paul knows how to be when he goes through being brought low.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-02.feedbackCorrect: He knows both extremes: brought low and honored.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the opposite extreme from what the question asks.
feedbackWrong.b: That is abundance of food, not being brought low.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-02.hint: Look for the first extreme named in the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-03.question: According to Philippians 4:12, what has Paul already experienced in life?
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-03.feedbackCorrect: Both sides of life entered his experience.

feedbackWrong.a: Inheritance is not cited: he speaks of experience.
feedbackWrong.b: He also cites being honored and abundance.
feedbackWrong.d: He also cites hunger and scarcity, not only plenty.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-03.hint: Pay attention to the pairs of opposites.

options.c: Plenty and hunger, abundance and scarcity
options.d: Only plenty, never going through need

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.question: Put Philippians 4:12 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.learningObjective: Recognize the order of the extremes named.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.feedbackCorrect: Brought low, honored, and the extremes of plenty and hunger.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the first "sei o que é" of the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-04.hint: The list begins with being brought low.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.question: In Philippians 4:11, how did Paul learn to live in any situation?
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.learningObjective: Remember the central word of contentment.
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.feedbackCorrect: Neither plenty nor lack takes that state from him.

feedbackWrong.a: He speaks and writes about this; he did not stay silent.
feedbackWrong.c: Anxiety is the opposite of what he learned.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-05.hint: It is the name of this whole scene.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-06.question: What does Philippians 4:11 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-06.feedbackCorrect: Help gladdens him, but his contentment does not depend on it.

feedbackWrong.a: He thanks openly, with no shame at receiving.
feedbackWrong.b: He rejoices at the help, with no despair at all.

filipenses-sem-fp-03-contentamento-06.hint: See what he says he learned.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.question: In Philippians 4:13–14, Paul thanks the church for sharing in his trouble, even while saying he can do all things in Christ.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.learningObjective: Understand strength in Christ together with receiving help.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.feedbackCorrect: Strength in Christ and gratitude for help go together in him.

feedbackWrong.false: He affirms both things, one in each verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-01.hint: Read the two verses as one speech.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.question: In Philippians 4:12, tap the little word that links plenty and hunger in the same experience.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.learningObjective: Recognize the link between the extremes lived.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.feedbackCorrect: The same life held both extremes named.

feedbackWrong.b: That summarizes circumstances, without linking the extremes.
feedbackWrong.c: That is one of the extremes, not the word that links them.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-02.hint: Look for the word that pairs with "quanto".

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.question: How does Philippians 4:11 help us understand "I can do all things" in 4:13?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.learningObjective: Relate Philippians 4:13 to its immediate context.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.feedbackCorrect: The context rules: all things are plenty and scarcity.

feedbackWrong.a: He just cited hunger and scarcity he lived.
feedbackWrong.b: Consumer desires do not appear in the passage.
feedbackWrong.d: He receives help with gratitude, not pride.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-03.hint: Look at the verses around the famous line.

options.a: A promise never to face need again
options.b: Power to get any object desired
options.c: Strength to live content in plenty and in lack
options.d: Ability to live without anyone's help

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.question: How does Paul's reasoning chain in Philippians 4:11–13?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.learningObjective: Understand the chain up to Philippians 4:13.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.feedbackCorrect: Learning, extremes lived, and the source of strength.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-04.hint: The source of strength closes the reasoning.

options.a: He learns contentment in any situation
options.b: He goes through plenty, hunger, and scarcity
options.c: He can do all things in the one who strengthens him

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.question: In Philippians 4:10, what did the Philippians finally do for Paul, according to him?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.learningObjective: Understand the renewed help from the Philippians.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.feedbackCorrect: Help returned because they remembered him again.

feedbackWrong.a: They already remembered before; opportunity was missing.
feedbackWrong.c: No judgment appears in this letter of gratitude.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-05.hint: It is the reason for his joy in the verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.question: What links Philippians 4:11 to 1 Timothy 6:8?
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.learningObjective: Relate contentment in two of Paul's letters.
filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.feedbackCorrect: Food and clothing suffice: contentment with enough.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts teach braking the chase for more.
feedbackWrong.b: Having little is no shame in either text.

filipenses-cam-fp-03-contentamento-06.hint: See what is enough in both texts.

options.b: Shame at having little in life

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-01.question: Philippians 4:13 promises that the believer can achieve any desire he has, without limits.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-01.feedbackCorrect: In context, all things is living in plenty and in lack.

feedbackWrong.true: Read 4:11–12 first: the strength is for contentment, not desires.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-01.hint: Check the immediate context of the line.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.question: In Philippians 4:13, tap the phrase that shows Paul's strength does not come from himself.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text the source of Paul's strength.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.feedbackCorrect: Strength is received from another: from the one who strengthens him.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the capacity, not its source.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the reach, not where the strength comes from.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-02.hint: Look for who gives, at the end of the verse.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.question: What reading do Philippians 4:11–12 support about contentment?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the passage supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.feedbackCorrect: Learned in Christ, he goes through both extremes.

feedbackWrong.a: He receives help gratefully: the things coexist.
feedbackWrong.b: He cites hunger and scarcity as real experience of his.
feedbackWrong.d: He feels and learns; it is not absence of feeling.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-03.hint: Join learning, extremes, and the source of strength.

options.b: Whoever has faith never faces real scarcity
options.c: It is possible to be whole in plenty and in lack, in him
options.d: Contentment is feeling nothing in the face of loss

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.question: What sequence reveals the sense of Philippians 4:10–13?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.learningObjective: See help, contentment, and Christ in the right order.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.feedbackCorrect: Help received, independent contentment, and strength in him.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the help that began arriving again.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-04.hint: The source of strength is the close of the passage.

options.a: The church remembers him and helps again
options.b: He declares contentment that does not depend on that
options.c: He points to Christ as the source of strength

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-05.question: In Philippians 4:12, which extreme of lack does Paul say he already knows by experience?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-05.feedbackCorrect: His contentment was tested precisely in lack.

feedbackWrong.b: That is recognition, not material lack.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the extreme of surplus, not of lack.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-05.hint: It is the opposite of abundance at the end of the list.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.question: What links Philippians 4:13 to 2 Corinthians 12:9?
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.learningObjective: Link the strength of Philippians to Paul's thorn.
filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.feedbackCorrect: In both, God's power shows itself precisely in weakness.

feedbackWrong.b: The strength is his in us, not self-sufficiency.
feedbackWrong.c: Weakness becomes a place of grace, not of punishment.

filipenses-pro-fp-03-contentamento-06.hint: See where God's power is made perfect.

estudo:fp-03-contentamento.context: Paul gives thanks because the Philippians began helping him financially again, after a time without opportunity. Before they think he depends on money to be well, he explains what he learned.
estudo:fp-03-contentamento.focusQuestion: What would change if what you have today were enough for you?
estudo:fp-03-contentamento.keywordGloss: It is not resignation: it is living whole in plenty and in lack, strengthened by Christ.
facts: Paul rejoiced because the Philippians finally remembered him.
He learned to live content in every and any situation.
He knows what it is to be brought low and also to be honored.
He has already had experience of plenty and hunger, abundance and scarcity.
He can do all things through the one who gives him strength.
The Philippians sent help twice when he was in Thessalonica.
